issues.legal_issue: A Rent Controller acting as a statutory authority and persona designata cannot condone delay in an application for leave to contest a special eviction petition when the governing statute gives no power to extend the filing period.
material_facts: A landlord sought eviction under the special procedure for a non-resident Indian owner, and the tenant was summoned to apply for leave to contest within the prescribed 15-day period.
The tenant filed the leave application one day after that period expired and sought condonation of the delay under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
The Rent Controller was appointed by the State Government, was a member of the State civil service, and had no statutory authority to extend the time for filing the leave application.
issues.conclusion: The Rent Controller had no jurisdiction to condone the delay, and rejection of the late leave application was not an error of law.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 13-B and 18-A(2) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, a tenant must apply for leave to contest within the period specified in the summons. The Act gives the Rent Controller no power to extend that period. Because the Rent Controller is a statutory authority and persona designata, rather than a court, Section 5 of the Limitation Act cannot confer that power; Section 29(2) does not make it available in these circumstances. The special procedure is a complete code to the extent stated in Prithipal Singh v. Satpal Singh. Mukri Gopalan v. Cheppilat Puthanpurajil Aboobacker was distinguishable because the appellate authority there was a court. Prakash H. Jain v. Marie Fernandes supports the conclusion that a statutory authority lacking power to condone delay must act within its statutory powers. Gaya Prasad Kar v. Subrata Kumar Banerjee did not assist the tenant insofar as the statute considered there specifically empowered the Rent Controller to extend time for rent deposits.

rule.if: special_eviction_leave_proceeding and leave_application_filed_after_deadline and decision_maker_is_persona_designata and governing_law_grants_no_power_to_extend_deadline

predicates.special_eviction_leave_proceeding: The matter is a special eviction proceeding in which a tenant must obtain leave to contest.
predicates.leave_application_filed_after_deadline: The tenant filed the application for leave to contest after the period specified for filing it had expired.
predicates.decision_maker_is_persona_designata: The decision-maker is a statutory authority acting as a designated person rather than as a court.
predicates.governing_law_grants_no_power_to_extend_: The law governing the proceeding does not empower the decision-maker to extend the filing deadline.

issues.definition: When a tenant files late for leave to contest a special eviction proceeding before a designated statutory authority, and the governing law gives that authority no power to extend the deadline, the delay cannot be condoned and the late application must be rejected.
